title: the server ends with the session of its client
intent: The first half of wave 42 of the plan of the owner (docs/PLAN.md 18.2).  The defect: the process of the ACP server outlived the agent.  A client that kept the pipe of the server open after the last turn left a process of Emacs behind, and nothing closed it: the protocol has no way to say that the client will not ask for more work, so the server over stdio waited for the end of the file that the client was never going to send.  What changes: the core answers the request `session/close' -- the method of ACP that the orchestrator calls when it closes the session of the agent (`packages/plugin/src/server/acp-internal/connection.ts:690-698', and the error of the answer is swallowed there, so a core that does not know the method keeps its session and its process alive without a word).  The request ends the session: the turn that runs in it is cancelled, the session leaves the registry of the server and its listener is dropped.  The server over stdio serves one client alone, so the end of that session is the end of the server: the process returns from its loop and ends without waiting for the client to close the pipe.  The server over a socket serves many clients, so the end of the session of one of them ends that session and not the server.  The check of the wave starts a real server process over stdio, drives a turn, closes the session with the request and keeps the pipe of the client open; the process must be gone within ten seconds, the answer of the request must leave before the server stops, and the second case of the check proves that the server over a socket keeps serving the clients that are still there and that the session that is over answers no prompt.  The second half of the wave (the spin of a server whose provider went silent) is not this wave: it is wave 54, with its own claim, and nothing of the loop on the path of the live request of the provider was measured here.
objection: The wave changes the life cycle of the process: a client that closes the session and wants to open another session on the same pipe gets a closed pipe.  A client that wants to keep the server has to keep its session, and `session/close' says the opposite.  The method is a part of ACP, so a client that does not call it is unaffected, and a client that calls it and swallows the answer, as Paseo does, gets what it asked for.  The wave does not prove the life cycle with the plugin of Paseo (`yeah-provider', outside this repository): the client of the check is an offline client that speaks the same JSON-RPC over the same two transports.  The wave does not change the transport of the primary deployment (a local socket), where the server must not end when one client leaves: that half is proven by the second case of the check.  The wave does not touch the spin of a server whose provider went silent: that is wave 54, and the claim of it is not registered here.
refuted_by: the server is still alive ten seconds after the client closed its session and kept the pipe open, or the server over a socket ended with the session of one client, or the session that is over answered a prompt, or the control of the claim does not make the check fail by its own assertion
note: Two sources of the wave contradicted each other and the contradiction is written down here.  The live run of the self-development copy (session wave42-2, 2026-11-18) implemented the end of the session as the notification `session/exit' -- a name of its own, not a part of ACP -- and the copy of that work is the wave file that came with the copy.  The plan of the integration with the orchestrator (docs/PASEO-INTEGRATION-PLAN.md 3.6) names `session/close' as the method that Paseo really calls, and the client of Paseo swallows the error of the answer: a core that knows only `session/exit' is never asked for it and keeps the process of the server alive exactly as before, which is the defect of the wave.  The wave therefore takes the method of ACP, `session/close', and the notification of the copy is not carried over.  The implementation of the method was written in the shared working tree by the parallel session of the integration with Paseo and was accepted into this wave after the check of the wave was run against it: the check passes in the tree of the wave (4.3 seconds) and the control of the claim (`sed -i 's/(setq yeah-acp--last-session-closed t)/(setq yeah-acp--last-session-closed nil)/' lib/yeah-acp.el') was applied to a copy of the tree and bit: the check ended with the code 1 and with its own words (`server-exit: the server is still alive ten seconds after the end of its session (pid ...)').  The live run of the copy itself ended before the work was over: the context of the run overflowed twice and the model wrote no summary, so nothing of that run is evidence of this wave; the evidence is the check of the wave and its control.
